content.summary: Reference list focusing on analgesia (morphine, nitrous oxide), antiplatelet agent interactions (P2Y12 receptor inhibition, ticagrelor), and outcomes in acute coronary syndromes including ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) and PCI.

references.citation: Stewart RAH, Jones P, Dicker B, Jiang Y, Smith T, Swain A, et al. High flow oxygen and risk of mortality in patients with a suspected acute coronary syndrome: pragmatic, cluster randomised, crossover trial. BMJ 2021;372:n355.
references.topic: oxygen therapy and mortality in suspected acute coronary syndrome

references.citation: Henrikson CA, Howell EE, Bush DE, Miles JS, Meininger GR, Friedlander T, et al. Chest pain relief by nitroglycerin does not predict active coronary artery disease. Ann Intern Med 2003;139:979–986.
references.topic: nitroglycerin and diagnostic utility for coronary artery disease

references.citation: Charpentier S, Galinski M, Bounes V, Ricard-Hibon A, El-Khoury C, Elbaz M, et al. Nitrous oxide/oxygen plus acetaminophen versus morphine in ST elevation myocardial infarction: open-label, cluster-randomized, non-inferiority study. Scand J Trauma Resusc Emerg Med 2020;28:36.
references.topic: analgesia comparison (nitrous oxide/acetaminophen vs morphine) in STEMI

references.citation: Silvain J, Storey RF, Cayla G, Esteve J-B, Dillinger J-G, Rousseau H, et al. P2Y12 receptor inhibition and effect of morphine in patients undergoing primary PCI for ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction. The PRIVATE-ATLANTIC study. Thromb Haemost 2016;116:369–378.

Circulation 2020;141:1354–1356.
references.topic: impact of morphine ± metoclopramide on ticagrelor platelet inhibition in AMI

references.citation: Stiermaier T, Schaefer P, Meyer-Saraei R, Saad M, de Waha-Thiele S, Pöss J, et al. Impact of morphine treatment with and without metoclopramide coadministration on myocardial and microvascular injury in acute myocardial infarction: insights from the randomized MonAMI trial. references.topic: morphine ± metoclopramide effects on myocardial and microvascular injury in AMI

references.citation: Kubica J, Adamski P, Ostrowska M, Sikora J, Kubica JM, Sroka WD, et al. Morphine delays and attenuates ticagrelor exposure and action in patients with myocardial infarction: the randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled IMPRESSION trial. Eur Heart J 2016;37:245–252.
references.topic: morphine reduces ticagrelor exposure and action in myocardial infarction

clinical_implications: Morphine administration in acute myocardial infarction (particularly STEMI) is repeatedly associated with delayed or reduced effectiveness of oral P2Y12-targeting antiplatelet agents (e.g., ticagrelor).
Studies investigate coadministration of prokinetic agent metoclopramide to mitigate morphine-induced delays in ticagrelor absorption/effect.
P2Y12 receptor inhibition is a central pharmacologic target discussed in relation to primary PCI and antiplatelet therapy effectiveness.

Associated Conditions: patients undergoing primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI)
delayed or reduced platelet inhibition / delayed activity of oral antiplatelet agents
